TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  May 10, 2017

  CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIRMAN ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present: Chair Zuckerman, Aou, Combs, Lum, Munday, Pope, Vanden Bos,
  Wisot,

  Committee Members Absent: Scott

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT

  Greg Grammer, Assistant City Manager
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy, Willdan
  Deputy Rebecca Schuerger, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Lomita Station
  Sergeant Ricky Osburn, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Lomita Station

  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS moved, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT to approve:

  MINUTES OF THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING OF APRIL 6, 2016, AS
  PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. 702 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE – SHORT TIME LIMIT PARKING REQUEST
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a brief report on this item. A visit was made to Deep
  Valley Cleaners, who is in favor of short time limit parking. The Appetizer was not in favor of the
  short time limit parking since their patrons will park for longer periods of time. A site visit was done
  during a time period when the businesses were open and found that 80% of on-street parking and
  80% of parking behind the property was full. The RHE Municipal Code allows for green curb
  markings and this may help in encouraging patrons staying for longer periods of time to park
  elsewhere. There may be some impacts to the businesses across the street, but there are also
  businesses that would benefit from green curb parking.

  Chris Wijtowich, Resident, stated that she is a customer of the dry cleaners and also stated that
  since Coreology moved in, it is difficult to find parking. She is in support of green curb parking and
  stated that there should be more than one space approved.

  A discussion was held on this item.

  A request was made to re-paint T’s on the street to delineate the parking spaces. Assistant City
  Manager Grammer stated that this will be done administratively.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion and seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  VANDEN BOS to:

  Make a recommendation to the City Council to install 30 minute parking signs on the north
  side of Deep Valley Drive from 700 Deep Valley Drive to the first driveway east of 718 Deep
  Valley Drive and leave all other parking as existing.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  B. HIGHRIDGE ROAD AT COUNTRY LANE – PARKING RESTRICTIONS
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a brief report on this item. A site visit with the
  Homeowner’s Association was done at the time period when children are released from school and
  observed 15 to 20 vehicles parked on the west side of Highridge Road between Country Lane and
  the stop sign at Whitley Collins Drive/Hillcrest Manor. The vehicles interfere with the visibility of
  cross traffic upon exiting the neighborhood. The residents also requested red curb to remind
  motorist of the “no stopping zone”.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the recommendation is to install a “No Parking Any

Meeting Minutes Traffic & Safety  1
Committee May 10, 2017
   Time” zone and remove the “No Stopping Any Time” zone with installation of at least 50’ of red curb
  on both sides of Country Lane.

  Tom Warner, Board Member of Rolling Hills Park Estates Homeowners Association, stated that
  there are a lot of people who park on both sides of Country Lane at Highridge Road. Residents
  need a line of site as they exit the neighborhood. Mr. Warner stated that he is in support of this
  recommendation.

  A discussion was held on this item.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS made a motion and seconded by COMMITTEE
  MEMBER WISOT to make a recommendation to the City Council for:

  1) The installation of a “No Parking Any Time” zone and removal of the “No Stopping Any
  Time” zone on the west side of Highridge Road between Country Land and Whitley
  Collins Drive/Hillcrest Manor.
  2) The installation of at least 50’ of red curb on the west side of Highridge Road north and
  south of Country Lane; and staff to determine if 50 ft. of red curb is sufficient for visibility
  when exiting Country Lane.

  Motion carried (Ayes: 8 Noes: 0 Abstained: 1 Absent: 0)
  Chair Zuckerman abstained.

  C. WHITLEY COLLINS DRIVE NEAR RIDGECREST INTERMEDIATE SCHOOL – TRAFFIC
  CONCERNS
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a brief overview on this item. There is concern with
  views being blocked for pedestrians crossing Whitley Collins Drive at Stonecrest Road. At the
  crosswalk at Whitley Collins Drive and Stonecrest Road, there are various “crosswalk” signs. One
  suggestion was to install LED signs to gain driver’s attention or rectangular rapid flashing beacons.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the recommendation is to install rectangular rapid
  flashing beacons with push button activation and installation of in-roadway warning lights
  connected to push button activation.
  A discussion was held on this item.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion and seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  COMBS to make a recommendation to the City Council for:

  1) The installation of rectangular rapid flashing beacons with push button activation; and
  2) The installation of in-roadway warning lights connected to the push button activation
  at the yellow crosswalk on Whitley Collins Drive at Stonecrest Road.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  D. PENINSULA HERITAGE SCHOOL – SCHOOL SIGNS
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a brief overview on this item. An intermediate school
  for Peninsula Heritage School was recently added to St. Luke’s Church campus and request was
  received from the Facilities Director to review the signage on Rolling Hills Road. In a site visit, it
  was determined that the signs need to be relocated in order to include the St. Luke’s campus.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the recommendation is the relocation of existing signs
  as appropriate to include the St. Luke’s Campus; to relocate a sign on Palos Verdes Drive North to
  bring it to a more visible location; and to add additional signs on Palos Verdes Drive North to identify
  the school speed limit ahead.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion and seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS
  to make a recommendation to the City Council for:

  1. The relocation of existing Assembly C and Speed Limit 35 signs on Rolling Hills
  Road (Exhibits E and F);
  2. The relocation of existing Assembly C sign on Palos Verdes Drive North (Exhibit G);
  3. The installation of SW24-3(CA) for southbound traffic on Rolling Hills Road (Exhibit H);
  4. The installation of SW243(CA) signs on Palos Verdes Drive North for Peninsula Heritage
  School and Dapplegray Elementary School (Exhibit I); and
  5. The installation of SW23-3(CA) signs on Palos Verdes Drive North for Rancho Vista
  Elementary School (Exhibit J).

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  Committee Member Munday stated that he would like staff to look into the location of the Montessori
  pre-school to be sure it is included in the relocated signs on Rolling Hills Road. Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she will look into it.

Meeting Minutes Traffic & Safety  2
Committee May 10, 2017
   E. CITY WIDE TRUCK ROUTE SIGNS
  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a brief introduction on this item. Traffic Engineering
  Deputy Itagaki stated that in observing the truck route signs it would be helpful to relocate the signs
  onto the signal poles so they are visible to the truck drivers.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the recommendation is for the Traffic & Safety
  Committee to discuss, review the signs, and provide direction to staff.

  In a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Deputy Schuerger, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department, stated due to the amount of construction in the City, there is little compliance to
  oversized vehicle restrictions on Palos Verdes Drive North.

  A discussion was held on this item.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion and seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  VANDEN BOS to make a recommendation to City Council to:

  Approve staff’s recommendations regarding truck route signs; clarification on Municipal
  Code Section 10.28.060 with changes to the sign in Exhibit D-3 (Eastbound Palos Verdes
  Drive North at Crenshaw Blvd.) as appropriate; and a recommendation that signs be added
  and not relocated as appropriate.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  COMMITTEE REPORTS (Verbal Reports)

  Committee Member Lum made a suggestion to install signs for “single-file line” for bicyclists on Palos
  Verdes Drive North.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there is no legal requirement that bicyclists ride in a single
  line. Bicyclists can travel in the travel lane, even when there is a bicycle lane, as long as they are travelling
  the same speed as traffic. If there is no bike lane, the same rule applies. If the bicyclist is slower than
  traffic, they will need to travel as close to the right as possible. Bicyclists must be aware of the law allowing
  vehicles to pass.

  Sergeant Osburn, County of Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department, stated that the law states that bicyclists
  cannot impede the flow of traffic and stated that enforcement of bicycle laws tends to be difficult and met
  with confrontational situations.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS stated that vehicles are parking on Masongate across the marked
  equestrian crossing and horses cannot come through. Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that this
  will be brought to the attention of Code Enforcement.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that the Marloma Homeowner’s Association send their gratitude
  for the improvements that were made at the corner of Silver Spur Road and Marina Drive.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY added that there is some confusion as to how the “Yield” sign is working
  when crossing Palos Verdes Drive North. When crossing Palos Verdes Drive North from the northeast
  corner to the southeast corner, pedestrians are often ignored by westbound through traffic. There are two
  westbound through lanes merging into one lane beyond the intersection at Silver Spur Road. Westbound
  drivers don’t always look for the pedestrians crossing Palos Verdes Drive North. Assistant City Manager
  Grammer stated that the crosswalk was repainted to make it more visible.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN requested an accident report for the intersection at Silver Spur Road and Palos
  Verdes Drive North.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE requested an accident report for cyclists.

  COMMITTEE ITEMS / FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None

  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 7:46 p.m.
